**Andrew R. Jassy** (born January 13, 1968)[[5]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-nuwber-5)[[6]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-6) is an American business executive who is the [president](President_(corporate_title) "President (corporate title)") and [chief executive officer](Chief_executive_officer "Chief executive officer") (CEO) of [Amazon](Amazon_(company) "Amazon (company)"). Before being appointed by [Jeff Bezos](Jeff_Bezos "Jeff Bezos") and the Amazon board during the fourth quarter of 2020,[[7]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-7) Jassy served as the SVP and later as the CEO of [Amazon Web Services](Amazon_Web_Services "Amazon Web Services") from 2003 to 2021.[[8]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-8)

## Early life and education

Jassy is the son of Margery and Everett L. Jassy of [Scarsdale, New York](Scarsdale%2C_New_York "Scarsdale, New York").[[3]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-nytmar-3) Jewish[[9]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-yworld-9)[[10]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-10) with [Hungarian](Jasz_people "Jasz people") ancestry,[[9]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-yworld-9) his father was a senior partner in the [corporate law](Corporate_law "Corporate law") firm [Dewey Ballantine](Dewey_Ballantine "Dewey Ballantine") in New York City, and chairman of the firm's management committee.[[3]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-nytmar-3) Jassy grew up in [Scarsdale](Scarsdale%2C_New_York "Scarsdale, New York"), and attended [Scarsdale High School](Scarsdale_High_School "Scarsdale High School"),[[3]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-nytmar-3)[[11]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-11) where he played varsity soccer and tennis.[[12]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-wsj2-12)

Jassy graduated [cum laude](Cum_laude "Cum laude") from [Harvard College](Harvard_College "Harvard College") in government, where he was advertising manager of *[The Harvard Crimson](The_Harvard_Crimson "The Harvard Crimson")*, before earning an MBA from [Harvard Business School](Harvard_Business_School "Harvard Business School"). In 1989, he wrote in *The Crimson* that the newspaper should continue to publish advertisements from [Eastern Air Lines](Eastern_Air_Lines "Eastern Air Lines"), despite an ongoing [labor dispute](Labor_dispute "Labor dispute") there.[[13]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-13)[[14]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-Hook-14)[[15]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-bloomberg.com-15)

## Career

Jassy worked for five years after graduation before entering his MBA program as a project manager for a [collectibles](Collectable "Collectable") company, [MBI](Danbury_Mint "Danbury Mint"), and then he and an MBI colleague started a company and closed it down.[[14]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-Hook-14)[[16]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-auto2-16)

Jassy joined Amazon as a marketing manager in 1997[[12]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-wsj2-12) with several other Harvard MBA colleagues.[[16]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-auto2-16)[[14]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-Hook-14) In 2003, he and [Jeff Bezos](Jeff_Bezos "Jeff Bezos") came up with the idea to create the [cloud computing](Cloud_computing "Cloud computing") platform that became known as [Amazon Web Services](Amazon_Web_Services "Amazon Web Services"), which launched in 2006.[[17]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-wsj1-17) Jassy headed it and its team of 57 people.[[1]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-auto-1)

In 2016, Jassy was named Person of the Year by the *[Financial Times](Financial_Times "Financial Times")*.[[14]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-Hook-14) A month later, Jassy was promoted from senior vice president to chief executive officer of Amazon Web Services.[[18]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-18)[[15]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-bloomberg.com-15) That year Jassy earned $36.6 million.[[19]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-19)

For his work as chief executive officer of Amazon Web Services, Jassy earned a base compensation of $175,000 in 2020, plus a [restricted stock](Restricted_stock "Restricted stock") unit award of 4,023 shares (a value of $12,104,844.93 as of July 26, 2020[[20]](Andy_Jassy#cite_note-AMZNPrice-20))
